records.old: (c) The northward part of the engine velocity must equal the southward current of 8 km/h. If θ is the angle north of east, then 20 sin θ = 8, so sin θ = 0.4 and θ ≈ 23.6°. The captain should point the ferry about 23.6° north of east (a bearing of about 066.4°), not due east. The northward part of the engine then cancels the current's southward push, and the ferry's path is directed towards Mbita. The captain pre-compensates for the current instead of ignoring it.
records.new: (c) To stay on the line to Mbita the ferry must have no southward drift, so the northward part of the engine velocity must equal the southward current of 8 km/h. If θ is the angle north of east, then 20 sin θ = 8, so sin θ = 0.4 and θ ≈ 23.6°. The eastward part is 20 cos θ ≈ 18.3 km/h (cos 23.6° ≈ 0.917), so the crossing takes 60 ÷ 18.3 ≈ 3.3 hours (about 3 h 16 min), a little longer than the 3 hours it would take with no current. The captain should point the ferry about 23.6° north of east (a bearing of about 066.4°), not due east, and the ferry's path is then directed towards Mbita. The captain plans for the current instead of leaving it out.
